memos.headline: S02 and S07 Lead at New Highs While Broad Selloff Hammers Mid-Tier Names; S04 and S09 in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape today. S02 is printing at its 52-week high with RSI 71.5, +58% over 12 weeks, and massive relative strength vs SPY (+46% over 12w)—this is a parabolic leader and I want to stay long but acknowledge the overbought risk; a close below its 50d mean (~383) would change my view. S07 is similarly dominant (+77.5% over 26w, +28.7% rel strength 12w) with RSI at a more comfortable 58.5, though the +45.6% premium to its 200d mean is extreme and a pullback to ~895 (roughly the 50d area) would be healthy. On the weak side, S04 is -31.2% from its 52-week high, well below both moving averages (-16.7% vs 200d), and showing persistent negative relative strength—this is a broken chart. S09 is similarly ugly with -19.5% over 12 weeks, RSI 33.9, and catastrophic relative strength vs SPY (-31.6% over 12w), suggesting continued distribution. S06 stands out as the cleanest risk-adjusted long: only -1.8% from highs, above both averages, low ATR of 2.42%, and strong 4w relative strength of +14.3%.

views.note: Parabolic leader at 52w highs with dominant relative strength; would reassess on a close below ~383 (50d area).
Massive uptrend (+77.5% 26w) with RSI 58.5 still not overbought, but +45.6% above 200d is stretched; a break below 895 flips me neutral.
Cleanest chart in the universe: near highs, low vol, above both averages, strong 4w relative strength; a close below 310 (roughly 200d area) would change my view.
Broken structure at -31.2% drawdown, deeply below 200d mean, persistent negative relative strength; would need a reclaim above 410 to reconsider.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Deliver Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between companies with durable, expanding earnings power and those facing cash-flow compression. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, a 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% YoY on only $8.47B of total debt — this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin, 21.8% revenue growth, and 81.2% net income growth with minimal leverage ($14.79B debt). On the other end, S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth, compressing net margin to just 4.9% — I cannot pay for that trajectory. S02 is similarly sluggish at 2.0% revenue growth and flat earnings, though its 5.6% margin is at least stable. I would need to see margin stabilization or a revenue inflection in S09 and S02 before reconsidering.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, 210% net income growth, and minimal debt make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 21.8% revenue growth and 81% net income growth on very low leverage ($14.79B debt) signals durable earnings power.

22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth are healthy, but 14.6% net margin and $36.21B debt on $17.41B revenue imply high leverage.
33.1% net margin is attractive but $448.76B total debt dwarfs revenue; 10% top-line growth is adequate but not compelling enough to offset leverage risk.

Net income down 45.8% YoY with only 2.4% revenue growth and a 4.9% net margin signals clear cash-flow compression — I need margin recovery before engaging.
2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, 5.6% net margin, and $77.92B debt offer no earnings momentum; a revenue acceleration above mid-single digits would change my view.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months, down 75bp over the past year, but with CPI running at +4.2% YoY (May print 333.98), further easing looks unlikely near-term. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10bp over three months and flat YoY, which removes urgency for additional cuts. The 10y-2y spread has compressed 18bp over three months to just +0.31pp, signaling the market is pricing a slower growth trajectory and limited further rate relief. I have moderate conviction that this pause-with-sticky-inflation regime favors banks (net interest margins stabilize with a positively sloped but flattening curve), staples (defensive in a slowing-growth environment), and is a headwind for long-duration growth names that need lower discount rates. A CPI print below 3.5% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing and flip me more constructive on duration-sensitive growth.

views.note: Banks benefit from a stable fed funds rate and still-positive 10y-2y spread supporting net interest margins in a pause regime.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the flattening curve and sticky inflation point to slowing growth without imminent easing.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds with 10y yields at 4.38% and no near-term rate cuts likely given 4.2% YoY CPI.
Cyclicals are caught between a stable labor market and a flattening curve signaling slower growth; I lack conviction either way.
Energy is less rate-sensitive but the slowing growth signal from the compressing curve tempers upside; staying neutral.
High-multiple growth names face valuation pressure with the 10y at 4.38% and sticky inflation keeping the Fed on hold.

memos.headline: S05 and S06 Filing Clusters Signal Elevated Activity; S09 and S10 Post-Earnings Tone Negative
memos.body: I am seeing a notable divergence in filing intensity and sentiment signals across the universe. S05 has filed six 8-Ks since May 11 including material definitive agreements, bylaw amendments, and board changes—this volume of corporate action suggests a narrative shift that may not yet be fully priced. S06 similarly has seven filings in the window, with a fresh director departure on June 25 and two filings on June 24 including Reg FD disclosure, pointing to an evolving story. On the negative side, S09 and S10 both reported earnings with immediate negative price reactions (−1.0% and −1.8% respectively), and neither has shown any positive catalyst since; the tone around both names remains soft. S03's June 10 entry into a material definitive agreement creating a direct financial obligation is worth monitoring but I lack enough tone data to take a strong view.

views.note: Unusually high filing cadence with material agreements and governance changes suggests a positive narrative shift building beneath the surface.
Heavy filing volume including Reg FD and a fresh director departure on June 25 creates uncertainty; tone is mixed and I want to see more before committing.
Earnings-driven −1.8% price reaction on May 20-21 with no subsequent positive catalyst; tone remains soft over five weeks.

memos.headline: Collapsing Oil Prices and Flattening Curve Signal Shifting Geopolitical Risk Landscape
memos.body: I see a mixed but notable geopolitical backdrop as of today. WTI crude has plunged 27.6% in one month to $72.67/bbl, which could reflect easing supply-side tensions (possible sanctions relief or OPEC+ discipline breakdown) — either way, this is a meaningful tailwind for energy consumers and a headwind for producers. The economic policy uncertainty index remains elevated at 273.74 but has fallen 13.9% over the past month, suggesting some near-term de-escalation in trade or regulatory policy risk even as the structural level stays high. The VIX at 18.89 has risen 13.9% over the past month, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 12bp, hinting that markets are pricing in slower growth or renewed policy uncertainty ahead. S06 has been unusually active with five 8-K filings since early May — including two on June 24 — which could indicate material corporate developments tied to regulatory or geopolitical exposure, warranting close monitoring.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K filing cadence (five filings in ~7 weeks including Reg FD) suggests material developments, but without content detail I cannot determine if geopolitical exposure is positive or negative.

Three 8-K filings in under a month including Reg FD disclosure suggest active corporate communication, but the sharp oil price decline and elevated policy uncertainty make directional conviction low without more detail.
Only a single Reg FD filing in May and no further disclosures; the falling oil price environment may be relevant depending on sector exposure, but I lack specifics to take a directional view.

June 18 8-K (Other Events) is the sole recent filing; with policy uncertainty still structurally high at 273.74 and the yield curve flattening, I stay neutral pending clarity on any geopolitical or regulatory catalyst.
Single 8-K on June 12 provides limited signal; the rising VIX and compressing term spread suggest caution, but no specific geopolitical catalyst is identifiable.
May Reg FD disclosure is the only filing; without content or sector-specific geopolitical exposure data, I have no basis for a directional call.
